items.action: Abrantes, between the Zêzere mouth and Belver dam, is a second agricultural-industrial hub with traditions, served by roads E.N. 2 and 3.

items.action: Products from inland regions could be shipped down the Tejo through a river port at Rossio, possibly combined with rail.
items.conditions: Possible, with Beira Alta links

items.action: The region has had manufacturing from Tramagal to Mouriscas, including metalworking, chemicals, milling and ceramics.
Proposes an industrial pole centred on Abrantes, including Tramagal, Rossio, Alferrarede, Mouriscas and Alvega, with development resting on Tagus navigation and the Almourol dam and lake.
items.conditions: Development base is navigation of the Tagus and the Almourol dam and lake
items.place: Abrantes, Tramagal, Rio de Moinhos, Rossio, Alferrarede, Mouriscas, Alvega, lago

items.action: Suggests tourism on the Almourol lake, wood industries, and agricultural canning could keep the Constância-to-Belver dam area busy within a few years.
items.cargo: agricultural raw material from neighbouring Alto Alentejo farms
items.place: Constância to Belver dam, lago de Almourol

items.action: Describes a planned third economic pole on the Quaternary lands of the Porto do Tejo, extending to the planned International Tagus dam site just downstream of the Sever.
items.conditions: Gently undulating terrain, aimed at agriculture and forestry

items.action: Describes the Tagus between Belver and Porto do Tejo as hemmed by steep hills, with poor road access and no room for industry; the railway runs along the valley.
items.conditions: Steep escarpments; stations cut into the hillside
items.place: Belver, Amieira, Fratel, Porto do Tejo

items.action: The Fratel dam, upstream of the Figueiró stream mouth, forms a lake with depth and width for river boats to navigate several kilometres above Porto do Tejo.
items.boat: barcos próprios para a navegação fluvial
items.conditions: Lake with large-radius curves ending almost at the border
items.place: Fratel dam, ribeira de Figueiró, Porto do Tejo

items.action: The Fratel dam is planned to provide energy, navigation, a road bridge and irrigation water for the Alto Alentejo scheme, and to aid the Monte Claro uranium mines.
items.conditions: Alto Alentejo scheme already approved
items.place: Fratel dam, Monte Claro, Alto Alentejo

items.action: Notes the Portas do Ródão and castles of great national historical importance on this stretch, with other defensive structures nearby.
items.place: Portas do Ródão, Flor da Rosa, Nisa, Marvão, Castelo Branco, Monsanto

items.action: Defines the upper Tagus industrial pole's zone of influence, about 100 km in radius, from the serra da Estrela to the Zêzere and the border, including part of Alto Alentejo.
items.place: serra da Estrela, Zêzere, Alto Alentejo

items.action: Describes regional industries: Covilhã as the country's largest wool centre, Portalegre growing, Castelo Branco with metalworking, milling and granite quarrying, and possible textile and embroidery expansion.
States that the region's fundamental economic base is its large forest resources, notably pine products such as cellulose, paper, resins, oils and essences, with export potential.
items.cargo: pine products: cellulose, paper, resins, oils, essences
items.place: region within 100 km of Porto do Tejo
